subject: Decoupled seat-credit model & token anchoring — RFI clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@orionhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFP — clarifications on hybrid seat + consumption model and credits

Karthik,

Thanks for the earlier response to Section 4 of our RFP. A couple of clarifications from procurement before we complete internal scoring — we attached Section 4 (Orion_RFP_Section4.pdf) with inline line numbers for reference. High-level asks: can you confirm how Redwood would price a hybrid model where we purchase dedicated seats for named users (for SLAs and guaranteed concurrency) but have those seats optionally convert to token credits for high-volume automated jobs? Specifically:

- Do seat "credits" convert to token bundles? If so, what is the conversion and how are model families (gen vs embeddings) priced against a seat credit?
- Is it possible to "anchor" a discount to the committed seat footprint (i.e., discounts scale with seats rather than token commit)?
- How do you handle overages for token consumption beyond bundled credits — simple per-token overage, tiered ladder, or blended rate?
- Do reserved GPU/Dedicated capacity credits offset token-billing on the invoice (and how are they applied across regions)?
- What smoothing / true-up windows do you support for variable usage? (monthly/quarterly/rolling 90-day?)
- If we reduce seats mid-quarter, how is proration handled for both seat fee and any associated token credits?

Can you provide a worked numerical example (one month example with baseline seats, a burst job, and a quarterly true-up) so we can show cost predictability to our finance team? Also confirm whether Redwood supports negative-balance protection (a buffer of pre-paid burst credits) and whether those buffer credits expire.

We need this clarification in writing by EOD tomorrow (May 28) to make the procurement cut.

Thanks,
Alex Jones
Sourcing Manager — Orion Health Systems
procurement@orionhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: RFP — clarifications on hybrid seat + consumption model and credits

Alex —

Appreciate the detailed questions and the RFP section. Below is our high-level approach and a worked example; I attached a draft workbook (redwood_pricing_workbook_ORH.xlsx) with a configurable sheet so you can swap in your forecast. If you want, Ben and I can walk through the sheet on a short call.

Key principles (short answers):
1) Seat credits to token conversion — supported. We treat a seat credit as a bundle of token credits that is pegged to a baseline model family profile. Example mapping (configurable): 1 seat-credit = 250,000 generation tokens OR 1,000,000 embedding tokens. Seat credits are fungible but consume token credits at the family-specific multiplier.

2) Discount anchoring — supported. You can anchor a volume discount to either (a) committed token spend, (b) committed seats, or (c) a hybrid anchor (seat count * seat-to-token conversion). For Orion we recommend anchoring to the committed token-equivalent of seats so burst consumption aligns with economic protection.

3) Overages — tiered ladder. Once bundled credits are exhausted in a billing period, overages bill at per-token rates that step down with cumulative monthly consumption tiers. Overage rates shown in the workbook use three bands (0-5M tokens, 5M-50M, 50M+), with progressive discounts at higher volumes.

4) Reserved GPU / Dedicated credits — applied as invoice credits against token charges up to the capacity footprint of the reserved pool. In practice: if you have a reserved GPU pool that can handle X tokens/hr, any token consumption that is routed to that pool first draws down the pool-hour capacity. If reserved GPU capacity is underutilized, we apply a monetary credit to token charges (not to seat fees). Regional mapping is configurable; credits are applied regionally first, then globally.

5) Smoothing and true-up — rolling 90-day smoothing by default with quarterly contractual true-up. This means short-term bursts are accommodated by smoothing windows; at the quarter close we true-up to committed anchors and issue/collect credits. We can switch to calendar-month true-ups if your accounting prefers.

6) Proration on seat changes — seats added mid-billing period are prorated daily for both seat fee and the associated token-bundle credits. Seats removed mid-period result in the remaining period being creditable on a daily prorated basis back to the token-credit balance (not cash), with a quarterly reconciliation to settle net differences.

Worked example (one-month view):
- Baseline: 50 seats committed for May. Conversion: 1 seat = 250K gen tokens.
- Bundled token credits from seats = 50 * 250K = 12,500,000 gen tokens for the month.
- Committed anchor discount: 18% off list gen-token rate for token-equivalent of seats.
- Actual consumption in May: 18,200,000 gen tokens (2.9M tokens over bundled credits).
- Overage ladder (example rates): list base = $0.00012/token; Tier1 (0-5M) = $0.000115; Tier2 (5M-50M) = $0.000105. Overage billing for 2.9M would be at Tier1 rate (assuming cumulative monthly usage into that band).
- Invoice flow: seat fees (net of any seat-specific discounts) + token overage charges (net of reserved GPU credits if applicable).

Negative-balance protection / burst buffer: we support optional pre-paid buffer credits (example: buy a 5M-token buffer at a discounted rate). Buffer credits are consumed before overage billing and can be set to roll over for up to 12 months or expire at contract-defined milestones.

Open items for Orion to confirm:
- Preferred true-up cadence (quarterly default vs monthly).
- Whether buffer credits should be global or regionally partitioned.
- Forecast split: gen vs embedding consumption (workbook has a tab for this).

Next steps: Ben and I will follow up with a Dedicated-capacity interaction note to explain reserved GPU credit application and provide the final workbook. If that looks good, we can produce a redlineable commercial appendix for Section 4.

Best,

Alex / Karthik,

Following up with a couple of operational clarifications around Dedicated capacity credits and an illustrative numeric flow you can drop into your procurement memo. Quoting Karthik below for context:

> "Reserved GPU / Dedicated credits — applied as invoice credits against token charges up to the capacity footprint of the reserved pool."

Operational detail: reserved GPU credits map to compute-hours on the dedicated pool. When a request is processed on the dedicated pool it consumes compute-hours and reduces the reserved-credit balance. If a request is routed off-pool (fallback) due to capacity shaping, that consumption is charged as tokens and will not automatically consume reserved GPU credits. You can request a hard-route policy so all eligible traffic consumes the reserved pool first (we typically recommend soft routing with high-priority routes for named user interactive traffic).

Example (monthly):
- Reserved pool purchased: 20 GPU-month equivalents. We estimate that under your model-family mix this maps to ~6.5M gen tokens/month of capacity handled on-pool.
- May usage (from Karthik example): 18.2M gen tokens total. Of that, 6.5M consumed on-pool (charged to reserved pool), 11.7M consumed off-pool (charged to token bundle / overage).
- Invoice credits: the reserved pool cost is invoiced as a seat/reserved-capacity fee. We apply a consumption offset credit to token charges equal to the monetary value of pool-handled consumption (not a per-token subtraction). Net effect: you don't pay both full pool fee and full token charge for the same on-pool consumption.

Proration nuance for seat reductions:
- If seats are reduced mid-month, we prorate the token-bundle credits daily and place the prorated token credit remainder into a contract account balance. That balance can be consumed for up to the next quarter, after which an unconsumed balance is subject to the quarterly reconciliation policy (might be credited or forfeited depending on the negotiated clause).

Buffer credit (negative spill) recommendation:
- For Orion we suggest a 5M-token buffer that rolls monthly for 12 months. That buffer acts as a surge absorber and is consumed before hitting the overage ladder. It provides one-month of cushion for predictable peaks and simplifies finance forecasting.

If you want a second worked example where reserved GPU pool handles a larger share (e.g., 10M tokens), I can add a sheet to the workbook.

—Ben

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and everyone for the clear operational notes. To summarize the commercial position we will put into the Section 4 appendix (so the procurement/compliance teams see one page):

1) Seat-credit conversion: 1 seat = 250K gen tokens (default), 1 seat = 1M embedding tokens. Configurable per-signature.
2) Discounts: Anchor to token-equivalent of committed seats (recommended for Orion) with a starter anchor discount of 18% off list gen-token price for the seat-equivalent bucket.
3) Overages: Tiered ladder with progressive volume discounts; buffer credit consumed prior to overage.
4) Reserved GPU credits: applied as invoice offsets to token charges for on-pool consumption; regional mapping available.
5) Smoothing / true-up: rolling 90 days with contractual quarterly true-up (option to change to calendar-month).
6) Proration: daily proration for mid-period seat adds/removals; unused prorated token credits held in contract account and reconciled quarterly.

Action items / timeline:
- We will provide a populated commercial appendix (Section4_Commercial_Appendix_ORH.docx) and the final pricing workbook (redwood_pricing_workbook_ORH.xlsx) by EOD Monday, 31 May.
- Schedule a 45-minute commercial walk-through with your finance and SRE leads on Wed, 2 June (suggest 10:00 PT) to step through the workbook and a sample true-up. Please confirm attendees and preferred time.
- If procurement wants tighter protections on buffer-credit expiry, we can add a simple 6/12-month rollover clause in the appendix.

If that all looks good I'll ask Legal to produce a redlineable appendix with the above terms and the numeric examples embedded.
